title: 7 links that explain the rest of today's software selloff. Intuit fell6% — is this a real reset?
author: tickeron_community
selftext:
The software selloff kept rolling. Intuit fell 6% and SAP and  
Atlassian 5% each as investors cut risk across application software,  
and SharonAI slid 6% on a revenue miss. On the other side, the average  
analyst target on Cadence sits 32% above the price. Here's today's  
second look at the software wreckage — who's getting cut, and who  
still has fans.  
  
Here is the rundown, drawn from today's write-ups.  
  
\*\*1. Intuit (INTU)\*\* — INTU dropped -6.02% to $324.77 from Monday's  
close of $345.56, a decline of -$20.79, with the selling occurring  
during Tuesday's regular session after shares opened lower. The move  
was sector-driven, not company-specific: application-software names  
sold off as the 10-year Treasury yield held near 5.1% and investors  
cut AI exposure ahead of Nvidia's after-close results, with Salesforce  
(-6%) and Workday...  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-intuit-intu-stock-down-6-02-today-39877/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-intuit-intu-stock-down-6-02-today-39877/)  
  
\*\*2. SAP SE (SAP)\*\* — SAP's U.S. shares fell from Monday's close of  
$233.83 to $221.99 by late Tuesday morning in New York, a -5.06%  
decline recorded during regular trading hours. The company-specific  
trigger was the announced exit of Chief Customer Officer Thomas  
Saueressig, an executive board member since 2019, who will leave at  
the end of March 2027 to become CEO of IONOS; the disclosure came  
before the U.S. open.  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-sap-se-sap-stock-down-5-06-today-39870/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-sap-se-sap-stock-down-5-06-today-39870/)  
  
\*\*3. Atlassian (TEAM)\*\* — TEAM fell -5.01% in Tuesday's regular  
session, sliding from Monday's close of $149.94 to $142.43, with an  
intraday low of $140.45 after weakness that started in premarket  
trading. The move was sector-driven: investors sold seat-based  
application software on mounting fears that AI agents are undermining  
per-user subscription economics, with attention fixed on Anthropic's  
IPO expected Thursday.  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-atlassian-corporation-team-stock-down-5-01-today-39873/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-atlassian-corporation-team-stock-down-5-01-today-39873/)  
  
\*\*4. SharonAI (SHAZ)\*\* — SHAZ fell -6.41% to $18.84 from Monday's  
$20.13 close, with the decline taking place in Tuesday's regular  
session after shares already slid in Monday's post-earnings  
after-hours trading. The driver was a third-quarter revenue miss:  
$9.93M against roughly $26.9M consensus, with first material billing  
on \~30MW of capacity pushed out to January 2027 and a $373M contract  
terminated over customer credit concerns.  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-sharonai-holdings-shaz-stock-down-7-25-today-39757/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-sharonai-holdings-shaz-stock-down-7-25-today-39757/)  
  
\*\*5. ReposiTrak (TRAK)\*\* — ReposiTrak shares fell -5.09% in Tuesday's  
regular session, sliding from Monday's close of $7.27 to $6.90 shortly  
after the open. The drop followed fiscal Q1 2027 results released  
after Monday's close: EPS of $0.08 missed the $0.10 consensus, revenue  
of $5.78 million trailed the $6 million estimate and declined -3% year  
over year, and operating margin compressed to 28.7% from 31.7%.  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-repositrak-trak-stock-down-8-25-today-39773/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-repositrak-trak-stock-down-8-25-today-39773/)  
  
\*\*6. Cadence Design Systems (CDNS)\*\* — The central CDNS price target  
discussed here is $410 , the arithmetic mean of 24 current analyst  
price targets rounded to a reader-friendly level. Target, not a  
promise.  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/cadence-design-systems-cdns-and-the-path-to-the-410-consensus-target-with-32-upside-39488/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/cadence-design-systems-cdns-and-the-path-to-the-410-consensus-target-with-32-upside-39488/)  
  
\*\*7. Quantinuum (QNT)\*\* — Quantinuum shares rose +3.43% to $32.84 by  
9:58 a.m. ET on Tuesday, up +$1.09 from Monday's $31.75 close, with  
the gain occurring during the regular session. No verified news or  
fundamental catalyst found for the move; it is likely a technical  
rebound after four straight declines totaling about -26% from the  
$43.00 close on Nov. 10, in a stock whose average daily swing is  
roughly ±4%.  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-quantinuum-qnt-stock-up-3-31-today-39813/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-quantinuum-qnt-stock-up-3-31-today-39813/)  
  
Is this just a risk-off day in software, or the start of a longer reset?  
  
Not financial advice. Figures are from today's (Nov 17) write-ups,  
using intraday or latest-close prices, not live quotes. Price targets  
are targets, not promises.
